title: Data Structures

cards.prompt: Define Abstract data type. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A set of logical values and permitted operations specified independently of how state is stored.

cards.prompt: An initially empty dynamic array has capacity 1 and doubles when full. Count each element write/copy as constant work. Give the total work for m appends, the amortized cost, and the worst cost of one append; explain why.
cards.definition: For m>=1 appends, ordinary writes cost m and resize copies form 1+2+4+... up to the last copied capacity, totaling less than 2m. Thus total work is O(m) and append costs O(1) amortized over the whole sequence. One append that resizes n stored elements still costs Theta(n). No input randomness or exclusion of resize operations is needed.
required_concepts: Account for all ordinary writes and the geometric sum of resize copies, giving O(m) total work.
Conclude O(1) amortized per append while a resizing append can take Theta(n) work.
accepted_variants: There are m ordinary writes and fewer than 2m copied elements across doublings, so O(m) total and O(1) amortized. A single resize with n elements still takes Theta(n).
major_error_concepts: Only non-resizing appends count in the average, so every append including resizing has worst-case O(1) cost.

cards.prompt: Define Array index invariant. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.

required_concepts: The valid-index relation 0<=i<length and mapping from logical positions to physical slots.
major_error_concepts: Using 0<=i<=length for ordinary element access.

cards.prompt: Define Binary-search insertion tradeoff. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.

cards.prompt: Define Circular-buffer representation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.

required_concepts: A fixed-capacity array plus head and size or head and tail state mapping a logical sequence across wraparound.
major_error_concepts: Reading only the contiguous suffix from head to capacity.

cards.prompt: For a circular buffer of capacity C>0 and head index h, map logical offset i to a physical array index. Assume 0<=h<C and 0<=i<size<=C. Evaluate C=5, h=4, i=2.
cards.definition: The physical index is (h+i) mod C, with the nonnegative remainder convention. For C=5, h=4, i=2 it is 1. Taking i mod C alone forgets where the logical sequence starts; using logical size as the modulus confuses occupancy with capacity.
required_concepts: Use (h+i) mod C, not i mod C or modulo logical size.
For the stated values, the physical index is 1.
accepted_variants: Add the head before wrapping: (4+2) mod 5=1. In general physical=(h+i) mod C.
major_error_concepts: Use i mod C, so the example accesses physical index 2.
Use logical size rather than storage capacity as the modulus.

cards.prompt: Define Contiguous-slot model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.

required_concepts: The idealized representation where adjacent logical indices occupy adjacent fixed-width slots, enabling address arithmetic and locality claims under qualification.
major_error_concepts: Claiming every Python list element object is stored inline contiguously.

cards.prompt: Define Dynamic-array append. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.

cards.prompt: What is a fixed-factor geometric capacity-growth policy, and why is C -> C+1 not that policy even though (C+1)/C>1?
cards.definition: Starting from positive capacity, resize a full array from C to ceil(g*C) for a fixed constant g>1 independent of C; doubling is the usual example. Successive capacities then grow geometrically (up to rounding). In C -> C+1, the ratio is 1+1/C and approaches 1 rather than remaining a fixed factor. Repeated unit-cost copying under one-slot growth accumulates quadratic work over a long append sequence.
required_concepts: The growth multiplier is a fixed constant g>1 independent of capacity, with integer rounding handled.
C+1 has a size-dependent ratio tending to 1 and is not fixed-factor geometric growth.
accepted_variants: Doubling uses fixed g=2. Adding one uses ratio 1+1/C, which tends to 1, so being greater than one at each step is not enough.
major_error_concepts: C+1 is geometric growth with constant amortized append because every individual ratio 1+1/C is greater than 1.

cards.prompt: Define BST height-indexed cost. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The operation bound in tree height h, becoming logarithmic only when a maintained invariant bounds h by logarithm of n.
required_concepts: The operation bound in tree height h, becoming logarithmic only when a maintained invariant bounds h by logarithm of n.
major_error_concepts: Calling all BST lookup O(log n).

cards.prompt: Define BST insertion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The search-to-missing-link operation attaching a new node then repairing parent and metadata invariants.
required_concepts: The search-to-missing-link operation attaching a new node then repairing parent and metadata invariants.
major_error_concepts: Replacing 7 because 5 is less than it.

cards.prompt: Define BST leaf deletion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** BST leaf deletion removes a node with no children and updates its parent link or the root while preserving ordering and stored metadata.
required_concepts: BST leaf deletion removes a node with no children and updates its parent link or the root while preserving ordering and stored metadata.
major_error_concepts: Leaving parent.left pointing to freed or detached node.

cards.prompt: Define BST minimum maximum and successor. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** BST minimum, maximum, and successor operations follow extreme-child paths and, for successor, the first qualifying ancestor under the search-tree invariant.
required_concepts: BST minimum, maximum, and successor operations follow extreme-child paths and, for successor, the first qualifying ancestor under the search-tree invariant.
major_error_concepts: Always returning the parent even when the parent key is smaller.

cards.prompt: Define BST one-child deletion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** BST one-child deletion splices the node's sole child into the deleted node's position while updating root and parent links.
required_concepts: BST one-child deletion splices the node's sole child into the deleted node's position while updating root and parent links.
major_error_concepts: Dropping the entire child subtree.

cards.prompt: Define BST search path. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The comparator-directed root-to-child path that either finds an equal key or reaches a missing child.
required_concepts: The comparator-directed root-to-child path that either finds an equal key or reaches a missing child.
major_error_concepts: Exploring both subtrees despite a valid total-order invariant.

cards.prompt: Define BST two-child deletion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** BST two-child deletion replaces or transplants the node with an in-order successor or predecessor while preserving both displaced subtrees and metadata.
required_concepts: BST two-child deletion replaces or transplants the node with an in-order successor or predecessor while preserving both displaced subtrees and metadata.
major_error_concepts: Attaching 7 directly and losing 5 or violating left-subtree order.

cards.prompt: Define Degenerate BST diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The valid ordered tree whose shape approaches a linked chain and defeats logarithmic operation claims.
required_concepts: The valid ordered tree whose shape approaches a linked chain and defeats logarithmic operation claims.
major_error_concepts: Calling the structure invalid merely because it is slow.

cards.prompt: Define In-order key sequence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The left-subtree then node then right-subtree enumeration used to expose binary-search order without implying balance.
required_concepts: The left-subtree then node then right-subtree enumeration used to expose binary-search order without implying balance.
major_error_concepts: Calling in-order enumeration breadth-first search.

cards.prompt: Define Left rotation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The local transformation promoting a node's right child while preserving the in-order sequence and reconnecting parent middle subtree root and metadata.
required_concepts: The local transformation promoting a node's right child while preserving the in-order sequence and reconnecting parent middle subtree root and metadata.
major_error_concepts: Moving y but dropping beta or leaving two parents.

cards.prompt: Define Node depth and tree height. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Node depth is the edge distance from the root, while tree height is the maximum downward edge distance under an explicitly fixed empty-tree and leaf convention.
required_concepts: Node depth is the edge distance from the root, while tree height is the maximum downward edge distance under an explicitly fixed empty-tree and leaf convention.
major_error_concepts: Mixing node-count and edge-count conventions mid-calculation.

cards.prompt: Define Right rotation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The mirror transformation promoting a node's left child while preserving in-order sequence and all ownership metadata.
required_concepts: The mirror transformation promoting a node's left child while preserving in-order sequence and all ownership metadata.
major_error_concepts: Swapping payloads while calling it a pointer rotation.

cards.prompt: Define Rooted binary tree. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A finite rooted node structure where each node has at most a distinguished left child and right child, independent of key order.
required_concepts: A finite rooted node structure where each node has at most a distinguished left child and right child, independent of key order.
major_error_concepts: Calling every binary tree a binary search tree.

cards.prompt: Define Single-versus-double AVL repair. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The rotation choice determined by the unbalanced node and heavy child's direction, with inner-heavy cases requiring two rotations.
required_concepts: The rotation choice determined by the unbalanced node and heavy child's direction, with inner-heavy cases requiring two rotations.
major_error_concepts: Applying one right rotation and retaining an inner-heavy violation.

cards.prompt: Define Subtree-size metadata. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A cached field equal to one plus left and right subtree sizes used only when every mutation repairs it.
required_concepts: A cached field equal to one plus left and right subtree sizes used only when every mutation repairs it.
major_error_concepts: Leaving an ancestor's size unchanged after insertion below it.

cards.prompt: Define Tree parent-child invariant. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The ownership and reciprocity rules for root parent null, child pointers, optional parent pointers, acyclicity and unique reachability.
required_concepts: The ownership and reciprocity rules for root parent null, child pointers, optional parent pointers, acyclicity and unique reachability.
major_error_concepts: Checking child links only while parent pointers disagree.

cards.prompt: Define Bottom-up heapify. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The linear-time construction sifting down internal nodes from the last parent toward the root.
required_concepts: The linear-time construction sifting down internal nodes from the last parent toward the root.
major_error_concepts: Sifting up every item and calling that the same linear construction.

cards.prompt: Define Extract-root operation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Heap root extraction saves the extreme root, moves the last item to the root, shortens the array, sifts the replacement downward, and returns the saved item.
required_concepts: Heap root extraction saves the extreme root, moves the last item to the root, shortens the array, sifts the replacement downward, and returns the saved item.
major_error_concepts: Deleting index zero and shifting all elements left without restoring heap structure.

cards.prompt: Define Heap insertion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Heap insertion appends the new key at the next complete-tree position and repeatedly sifts it upward until heap order is restored.
required_concepts: Heap insertion appends the new key at the next complete-tree position and repeatedly sifts it upward until heap order is restored.
major_error_concepts: Sorting the entire array after each insert and claiming heap insertion behavior.

cards.prompt: Define Heap parent and child indices. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The zero-based formulas parent=(i-1)//2 and children=2i+1,2i+2 when indices exist.
required_concepts: The zero-based formulas parent=(i-1)//2 and children=2i+1,2i+2 when indices exist.
major_error_concepts: Using one-based formulas without conversion.

cards.prompt: Define Heap partial-order boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The fact that heap order certifies only ancestor-child extremes and root access, not sorted iteration or fast arbitrary search.
required_concepts: The fact that heap order certifies only ancestor-child extremes and root access, not sorted iteration or fast arbitrary search.
major_error_concepts: Using array position to infer global rank beyond the root.

cards.prompt: Define Heap peek. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The constant root observation returning the extreme item without mutation under a nonempty contract.
required_concepts: The constant root observation returning the extreme item without mutation under a nonempty contract.
major_error_concepts: Scanning the whole heap because it is not sorted.

cards.prompt: Define Heap-versus-search-tree selection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The workload distinction between repeated extreme access and ordered search/range/predecessor operations.
required_concepts: The workload distinction between repeated extreme access and ordered search/range/predecessor operations.
major_error_concepts: Calling one universally faster from both having logarithmic updates.

cards.prompt: Define Implicit heap layout. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The complete-tree shape encoded by an array without explicit child pointers.
required_concepts: The complete-tree shape encoded by an array without explicit child pointers.
major_error_concepts: Leaving internal holes and still using standard index formulas.

cards.prompt: Define Lazy deletion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The technique marking old entries removed and inserting replacements while pop skips stale entries, with live mapping and compaction policy.
required_concepts: The technique marking old entries removed and inserting replacements while pop skips stale entries, with live mapping and compaction policy.
major_error_concepts: Returning the first stale entry because its priority is best.

cards.prompt: Define Linear heapify work argument. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The level-sensitive accounting where many nodes move little and few high nodes move far, summing to linear work.
required_concepts: The level-sensitive accounting where many nodes move little and few high nodes move far, summing to linear work.
major_error_concepts: Claiming every node sifts through log n levels.

cards.prompt: Define Max-heap convention. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The mirrored parent-not-less-than-child invariant whose root is maximal, kept separate from a min-heap API.
required_concepts: The mirrored parent-not-less-than-child invariant whose root is maximal, kept separate from a min-heap API.
major_error_concepts: Negating some priorities while also using max-heap operations and reversing twice.

cards.prompt: Define Min-heap invariant. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The partial order where every parent key is no greater than either child so the root is globally minimal.
required_concepts: The partial order where every parent key is no greater than either child so the root is globally minimal.
major_error_concepts: Requiring every earlier array element to be no greater than every later one.

cards.prompt: Define Priority-queue ADT. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A collection supporting insert and access/removal of the item with minimum or maximum specified priority plus empty and tie behavior.
required_concepts: A collection supporting insert and access/removal of the item with minimum or maximum specified priority plus empty and tie behavior.
major_error_concepts: Returning insertion order while calling it priority order.

cards.prompt: Define Priority-update strategy. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified choice among indexed handles, entry maps, decrease-key repair, remove-and-reinsert or lazy replacement.
required_concepts: The specified choice among indexed handles, entry maps, decrease-key repair, remove-and-reinsert or lazy replacement.
major_error_concepts: Changing a field and assuming future pop repairs it automatically.

cards.prompt: For Python min-heaps, compare heapreplace and heappushpop. Starting separately from [5,9,7], what does each return when the new item is 3, and what remains? What happens on an empty heap?
cards.definition: heapreplace removes and returns the old minimum, then installs the new item: with [5,9,7] and 3 it returns 5 and retains the multiset {3,7,9}. heappushpop has push-then-pop semantics: it returns the minimum of the old items and the new item, so here it returns 3 and retains {5,7,9}. heapreplace raises IndexError on an empty heap; heappushpop([],3) returns 3 and leaves the heap empty. Their return values can coincide for other inputs; the operations are not synonyms.
required_concepts: heapreplace returns 5 and retains {3,7,9}; heappushpop returns 3 and retains {5,7,9} for the stated independent heaps.
On an empty heap, heapreplace raises IndexError, while heappushpop returns the incoming item and leaves an empty heap.
accepted_variants: Replace gives back old min 5 and keeps 3,7,9. Push-pop gives back new min 3 and keeps 5,7,9. Empty replace raises IndexError; empty push-pop returns 3 and stays empty.
major_error_concepts: Both functions return 3 and keep 5,7,9, and both raise IndexError when the original heap is empty.

cards.prompt: Define Sift-down repair. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The downward exchanges of a violating parent with the more extreme child until heap order is restored.
required_concepts: The downward exchanges of a violating parent with the more extreme child until heap order is restored.
major_error_concepts: Always swapping with the left child.

cards.prompt: Define Sift-up repair. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The upward exchanges after insertion while a child violates heap order with its parent.
required_concepts: The upward exchanges after insertion while a child violates heap order with its parent.
major_error_concepts: Comparing only with siblings.

cards.prompt: Define Stable priority tie-breaker. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A monotone insertion counter or declared secondary key ensuring deterministic FIFO order among equal priorities and avoiding payload comparison.
required_concepts: A monotone insertion counter or declared secondary key ensuring deterministic FIFO order among equal priorities and avoiding payload comparison.
major_error_concepts: Using (priority,task) and allowing a payload comparison error on ties.

cards.prompt: Define Stale-entry compaction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The rebuild policy controlling physical heap growth when lazy-deleted entries dominate live entries.
required_concepts: The rebuild policy controlling physical heap growth when lazy-deleted entries dominate live entries.
major_error_concepts: Calling physical length the priority-queue logical size.

cards.prompt: Define Adjacency-list representation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The per-vertex collection of outgoing or incident neighbors/edges whose symmetry and duplicate behavior depend on graph policy.
required_concepts: The per-vertex collection of outgoing or incident neighbors/edges whose symmetry and duplicate behavior depend on graph policy.
major_error_concepts: Storing only a->b while claiming undirected neighborhood symmetry.

cards.prompt: Define Adjacency-matrix representation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The vertex-indexed table whose cell encodes edge existence count weight or reference under a declared graph policy.
required_concepts: The vertex-indexed table whose cell encodes edge existence count weight or reference under a declared graph policy.
major_error_concepts: Using a boolean matrix and claiming multigraph round-trip fidelity.

cards.prompt: Define Disjoint-set ADT. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A partition of elements supporting make-set, find-set and union while abstract membership is independent of chosen representative nodes.
required_concepts: A partition of elements supporting make-set, find-set and union while abstract membership is independent of chosen representative nodes.
major_error_concepts: Treating representative identity as the semantic block name.

cards.prompt: Define Disjoint-set amortized boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The qualified near-constant amortized sequence result for union by rank/size plus path compression, distinct from each operation's worst-case constant time.
required_concepts: The qualified near-constant amortized sequence result for union by rank/size plus path compression, distinct from each operation's worst-case constant time.
major_error_concepts: Calling every individual find worst-case O(1).

cards.prompt: Define Edge-list representation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The collection of edge records directly preserving each specified edge occurrence and attributes, with neighborhood queries generally requiring scans or indexes.
required_concepts: The collection of edge records directly preserving each specified edge occurrence and attributes, with neighborhood queries generally requiring scans or indexes.
major_error_concepts: Deduplicating them because endpoints match.

cards.prompt: Define Find-set. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The operation following parent links to a root and returning its representative while preserving partition semantics.
required_concepts: The operation following parent links to a root and returning its representative while preserving partition semantics.
major_error_concepts: Returning a because it is the queried element.

cards.prompt: Define Graph-representation cost matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The space and operation table indexed by vertex count V edge count E density directedness and cell/bucket representation.
required_concepts: The space and operation table indexed by vertex count V edge count E density directedness and cell/bucket representation.
major_error_concepts: Calling adjacency lists always smaller even for dense graphs with large per-edge overhead.

cards.prompt: Define Graph semantic contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The frozen vertex identity edge identity directedness multiplicity self-loop weight and attribute policy before choosing storage.
required_concepts: The frozen vertex identity edge identity directedness multiplicity self-loop weight and attribute policy before choosing storage.
major_error_concepts: Changing graph semantics during representation conversion.

cards.prompt: Define Parent-forest representation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The concrete encoding where each element points toward a root and roots identify current representatives without cycles.
required_concepts: The concrete encoding where each element points toward a root and roots identify current representatives without cycles.
major_error_concepts: Allowing a nonroot cycle and calling every node mutually representative.

cards.prompt: Define Path-compressed-trie boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The context where unary paths can be stored as multi-symbol edges while split/merge correctness and advanced integer structures remain downstream.
required_concepts: The context where unary paths can be stored as multi-symbol edges while split/merge correctness and advanced integer structures remain downstream.
major_error_concepts: Calling compression free without storing labels or handling partial matches.

cards.prompt: Define Path compression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The find-time rewrite making visited nodes point closer or directly to the root while leaving partition membership unchanged.
required_concepts: The find-time rewrite making visited nodes point closer or directly to the root while leaving partition membership unchanged.
major_error_concepts: Changing ranks as though compression were a union.

cards.prompt: Define Representation round-trip audit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The conversion check preserving the specified vertex set edge multiset directions loops weights attributes and identities across representations.
required_concepts: The conversion check preserving the specified vertex set edge multiset directions loops weights attributes and identities across representations.
major_error_concepts: Accepting equal edge count despite reversed directions or merged parallel edges.

cards.prompt: Define Representative nonidentity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The rule that roots may change after unions and are unsuitable as stable external labels unless separately canonicalized.
required_concepts: The rule that roots may change after unions and are unsuitable as stable external labels unless separately canonicalized.
major_error_concepts: Treating a representative change as element migration between blocks.

cards.prompt: Define Trie exact lookup. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The operation following one edge per key symbol and requiring a terminal marker at the final node.
required_concepts: The operation following one edge per key symbol and requiring a terminal marker at the final node.
major_error_concepts: Returning true for any existing prefix.

cards.prompt: Define Trie length-and-alphabet cost. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The operation cost indexed by key length and child representation rather than only number of stored keys.
required_concepts: The operation cost indexed by key length and child representation rather than only number of stored keys.
major_error_concepts: Calling lookup O(1) because tree height does not depend directly on number of keys.

cards.prompt: Define Trie prefix lookup. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The operation finding the node for a prefix then exposing or enumerating descendants under a separate output-cost contract.
required_concepts: The operation finding the node for a prefix then exposing or enumerating descendants under a separate output-cost contract.
major_error_concepts: Calling prefix lookup constant regardless of prefix length or returned keys.

cards.prompt: Define Trie terminal marker. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The state distinguishing a key that ends at an internal prefix node from a prefix that is not itself stored.
required_concepts: The state distinguishing a key that ends at an internal prefix node from a prefix that is not itself stored.
major_error_concepts: Treating every internal prefix as an inserted key.

cards.prompt: Define Trie. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A rooted prefix structure whose path labels encode key prefixes and whose terminal markers distinguish complete keys.
required_concepts: A rooted prefix structure whose path labels encode key prefixes and whose terminal markers distinguish complete keys.
major_error_concepts: Duplicating the entire prefix for every key.

cards.prompt: Define Union by size or rank. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The heuristic attaching a smaller or lower-rank root below a larger/higher root and updating only root metadata.
required_concepts: The heuristic attaching a smaller or lower-rank root below a larger/higher root and updating only root metadata.
major_error_concepts: Updating size on every member or attaching large under small while claiming the heuristic.

cards.prompt: Define Union operation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The operation merging two blocks by linking their distinct roots and doing nothing semantically when already united.
required_concepts: The operation merging two blocks by linking their distinct roots and doing nothing semantically when already united.
major_error_concepts: Linking arbitrary nonroot nodes and creating a cycle.

cards.prompt: Define AI cache-and-index application. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The bounded use of maps sets tries and graph representations for memoization deduplication prefix lookup and relation storage while eviction persistence privacy and semantic validity remain separate.
required_concepts: The bounded use of maps sets tries and graph representations for memoization deduplication prefix lookup and relation storage while eviction persistence privacy and semantic validity remain separate.
major_error_concepts: Treating a correct hash table as proof cache keys are semantically valid or safe.

cards.prompt: Define AI task-queue application. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The bounded use of queue deque and priority structures for research tasks while scheduling policy fairness durability retries and distributed execution remain systems concerns.
required_concepts: The bounded use of queue deque and priority structures for research tasks while scheduling policy fairness durability retries and distributed execution remain systems concerns.
major_error_concepts: Calling priority scheduling fair because heap operations are correct.

cards.prompt: Define Benchmark harness contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The controlled workload size distribution warmup repetitions environment versions measurement statistic and correctness precheck for empirical tradeoff evidence.
required_concepts: The controlled workload size distribution warmup repetitions environment versions measurement statistic and correctness precheck for empirical tradeoff evidence.
major_error_concepts: Timing one run with different initial data and calling it complexity proof.

cards.prompt: Define Complexity instrumentation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The counting of comparisons probes moves allocations pointer updates or other model events to connect traces with theoretical operation costs.
required_concepts: The counting of comparisons probes moves allocations pointer updates or other model events to connect traces with theoretical operation costs.
major_error_concepts: Using wall time alone to identify which operation caused scaling.

cards.prompt: Define Corrupted-state triage. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The process locating the earliest broken invariant, classifying semantic versus representation damage, preserving the receipt and repairing from an accepted valid state.
required_concepts: The process locating the earliest broken invariant, classifying semantic versus representation damage, preserving the receipt and repairing from an accepted valid state.
major_error_concepts: Editing the final size field to match reachable nodes without finding the lost node.

cards.prompt: Define Differential testing. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The execution of identical generated operation sequences against candidate and reference implementations with semantic results compared after each step.
required_concepts: The execution of identical generated operation sequences against candidate and reference implementations with semantic results compared after each step.
major_error_concepts: Comparing only final length after thousands of operations.

cards.prompt: Define Executable invariant assertion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A check over concrete state run at controlled boundaries to detect corruption near its cause without replacing proof or tests.
required_concepts: A check over concrete state run at controlled boundaries to detect corruption near its cause without replacing proof or tests.
major_error_concepts: Asserting only size>=0.

cards.prompt: Define Failure shrinking. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The reduction of a failing generated trace while preserving the same material invariant or semantic failure.
required_concepts: The reduction of a failing generated trace while preserving the same material invariant or semantic failure.
major_error_concepts: Deleting the operation that triggers the bug merely to make the test pass.

cards.prompt: Define Memory-and-indirection profile. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The accounting of payload storage spare capacity node links object overhead tombstones caches and transient copies under representative sizes.
required_concepts: The accounting of payload storage spare capacity node links object overhead tombstones caches and transient copies under representative sizes.
major_error_concepts: Using big-O space alone as an exact memory comparison.

cards.prompt: Define Metamorphic structure test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A relation among transformed inputs or operation sequences whose outputs should agree without requiring one expected output constant.
required_concepts: A relation among transformed inputs or operation sequences whose outputs should agree without requiring one expected output constant.
major_error_concepts: Assuming physical table layout must also return byte-for-byte identical.

cards.prompt: Define Operation-frequency profile. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The measured or estimated mix of lookups insertions deletions endpoint access range queries priority updates and iteration shaping a representation choice.
required_concepts: The measured or estimated mix of lookups insertions deletions endpoint access range queries priority updates and iteration shaping a representation choice.
major_error_concepts: Selecting from one rare operation while ignoring dominant costs.

cards.prompt: Define Ordering-and-multiplicity requirement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The contract for absent insertion sorted priority or stable order plus set map multiset or multimap duplicates.
required_concepts: The contract for absent insertion sorted priority or stable order plus set map multiset or multimap duplicates.
major_error_concepts: Discarding duplicates to gain a simpler representation.

cards.prompt: Define Persistence-and-concurrency handoff. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The boundary where in-memory mutable structures expose needs but durable transactions shared-memory synchronization reclamation and distributed replication belong to downstream owners.
required_concepts: The boundary where in-memory mutable structures expose needs but durable transactions shared-memory synchronization reclamation and distributed replication belong to downstream owners.
major_error_concepts: Adding a lock field and claiming crash-safe exactly-once delivery.

cards.prompt: Define Property-based operation sequences. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Property-based operation sequences are generated valid and invalid traces checked against general contracts and invariants across many structures and histories.
required_concepts: Property-based operation sequences are generated valid and invalid traces checked against general contracts and invariants across many structures and histories.
major_error_concepts: Generating only pushes and never exercising pop or empty state.

cards.prompt: Define Qualified data-structure conclusion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The narrow final statement joining ADT conformance invariant preservation operation costs tests measurements versions limitations and handoffs for one implementation.
required_concepts: The narrow final statement joining ADT conformance invariant preservation operation costs tests measurements versions limitations and handoffs for one implementation.
major_error_concepts: Calling passing tests and import proof of all-input correctness learner mastery or OpenAI research readiness.

cards.prompt: Define Randomized adversarial trace. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A seeded operation sequence biased toward boundaries collisions duplicates resizes empty/full cases skewed trees ties updates and conversion hazards.
required_concepts: A seeded operation sequence biased toward boundaries collisions duplicates resizes empty/full cases skewed trees ties updates and conversion hazards.
major_error_concepts: Calling uniform random inputs adversarial coverage.

cards.prompt: Define Reference model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A simpler trusted implementation of the same abstract contract used to compare operation results and logical state, not necessarily performance.
required_concepts: A simpler trusted implementation of the same abstract contract used to compare operation results and logical state, not necessarily performance.
major_error_concepts: Using a reference with different duplicate or ordering semantics.

description: A definition-recall course deck covering core concepts in Data Structures.
